_comment: Finding-level adjudication of run-4 on mt-test-studio @ 36972b38.
TWO PASSES, AND THEY DISAGREED. The first asked 'is the inefficiency real'. The second, run
independently with no sight of the first, also asked 'would the proposed code actually run' --
and that question overturned several verdicts. Spot-checked against source: finding 3's
proposal references an attribute that appears nowhere in the repository, and finding 9
replaces a queryset with a list that property_matrix() then calls .order_by() on. Both would
raise AttributeError. The second pass is authoritative here because its claims were checkable
firstPassVerdict is retained so the disagreement stays visible rather than being tidied away.
adjudicated is still false: two model passes agreeing is not a human confirming.
WHAT THIS EXPOSED. The value gate has no viability check. It tests for no-ops, wrong
direction, non-data-access, cold paths, immateriality and contradicted assumptions -- but not
whether the proposal references symbols that exist. Findings 3 and 9 are mechanically
adjudicatedBy: two independent model passes; second authoritative; pending human confirmation

verdicts.why: The loop at core/views.py:154 is a genuine per-product N+1, but the proposal only groups active-run counts and never replaces the cited TestExecution.aggregate() (lines 160-166); dropped as written the view breaks (agg undefined), and it adds a needless Product.objects.all() subquery. Unusable rewrite.
proposed/rationale/equivalenceArgument are all empty strings. No actionable change, and the cited exists() in the plan import loop is not addressed.

create_execution() (testruns/models.py:145-181) is not a thin insert: it resolves the assignee, queries TestExecutionStatus, reads case.history.latest() for the NOT-NULL case_text_version, expands the property matrix and inserts TestExecutionProperty rows. The proposal also references new_run.execution_model, which does not exist anywhere in the repo, so bulk_create would crash and would violate NOT NULL if it ran.

admin_views.py:949-958 already ends in .values_list("global_id", flat=True); the proposal only swaps map/filter for a list comprehension. Identical SQL, zero DB change, and the claimed over-fetch does not exist.

core/views.py:501-509 materializes every distinct TestExecution.case_id into a Python set and then feeds it back as pk__in; executed_case_ids is not used again in that view (lines 511-537), so pushing it into a subquery removes one round trip and the full id transfer.

testcases/views.py:352 iterates the queryset exactly once; wrapping it in list() issues the same single query. DB work identical, only Python-level explicitness changes (the rationale admits as much).
testplans/views.py:380-388 runs a values_list query to build run_ids and then a second aggregate; filtering on run__plan_id collapses this to one query with the same aggregate columns.

context_processors.py:36-48 iterates streams at line 48 (next(...) over it) inside the same function, so removing list() saves nothing and still executes one query. Worse, it moves evaluation outside the try/except OperationalError|ProgrammingError block that the comment says exists to stop 500-cascades on an unmigrated DB.

properties is a union() queryset and property_matrix() calls properties.order_by("name","value") (models.py:189). Passing list(...) as proposed raises AttributeError, so the rewrite is not runnable; the stated assumption that property_matrix accepts an evaluated iterable is false.

pk__isnull=False is an always-true predicate on a Django PK; it adds a redundant WHERE clause and changes no rows and no index choice. Explicit no-op (and the command is a cold management path anyway).

forms.py:364-367 executes no queries at all: plan_ids is a lazy values_list used as an IN subquery, and both querysets are only assigned to form fields. values_list("plan") and ("plan_id") produce identical SQL, and adding distinct() to a subquery does not reduce work. The claimed 'pulling whole plan objects' never happens.

testruns/views.py:315-322 does TestCasePlan.objects.get(plan=..., case=case) once per case inside the loop; batching into one filter(case__in=...) dict is a genuine N+1 fix. Note the proposal drops the matrix_type kwarg present at line 328, so it needs care.
admin_views.py:1046-1049 runs TestRun.objects.filter(global_id=...).exists() once per imported run inside the nested plan/run loops; one batched global_id__in lookup replaces N queries.
admin_views.py:1052-1060 issues a user lookup per tester-bearing run inside the import loop; a single username__in map removes the per-row query and username is unique on the default User model.

admin_views.py:1079-1084 does user_model.objects.filter(username=assignee_name).first() once per execution in the innermost loop — the highest-multiplicity N+1 in this importer. Batching is a genuine win.

core/views.py:186 runs TestCase.objects.filter(section__product=stream).count() inside the per-product loop; a single values_list("section__product").annotate(Count) grouped query yields the same integer per stream in one pass.
Same per-stream count inside the CSV export loop at core/views.py:598; the grouped precompute removes one query per product.

testplans/views.py:515 the exists() check is functional idempotency for the four fixed standard runs, not an inefficiency; deleting it creates duplicate TestRun rows (no unique constraint on plan+summary is added). Four indexed lookups is not a defect worth trading correctness for.
core/views.py:877-883 issues two count() queries per Section inside the loop; the grouped values("section_id").annotate(...) with a filtered Count replaces 2N queries with one.

One query before, one after. TestExecution.stop_date has db_index=True (testruns/models.py:310), so ORDER BY stop_date DESC LIMIT 1 can stop early while MAX() over the joined set is not obviously cheaper. Cannot defend a real reduction either way; it also leaves the surrounding per-stream loop untouched.
Same construct at core/views.py:587-594 in the CSV export loop; single query either way, indexed stop_date makes the ORDER BY/LIMIT plan competitive with MAX(). No demonstrable DB-work reduction.
core/views.py:856-865 issues four separate count() queries over the same TestCase/section__product filter; one aggregate with filtered Counts is 1 round trip and 1 scan instead of 4.
telemetry/api.py:28-31 runs two count() queries on the same distinct queryset; a single aggregate with two filtered distinct Counts returns both values in one round trip.

testcases/views.py:1073-1080 fires up to two sibling exists() queries on the same product/parent scope; one name__in query covers both candidates. Minor but genuine (saves a round trip whenever the desired name is taken).
core/views.py:512-520 is three count() queries over the same base filter; one aggregate with three filtered Counts is a real 3-to-1 round-trip reduction.

Splitting get(Q(email=value) | Q(username=value)) into two sequential filter().first() calls issues MORE round trips in the username-match case, and it also swallows MultipleObjectsReturned. The tool's own equivalence note concedes it is not equivalent.

kiwi_auth/admin.py:222 counts every superuser row; since the branch is already guarded by user.is_superuser, exclude(pk=user.pk).exists() is logically identical and lets MySQL stop at the first matching row instead of counting all. Small but genuine.
rpc/tests/test_testplan.py:321-325 is a real nested-loop count() N+1, but it lives in a test method, so it never runs in production.

kiwi_auth/tests/test_admin.py:220 asserts exactly one superuser remains. The proposal replaces that with filter(pk=self.admin.pk).exists(), asserted against 1 — a vacuous True==1 check that destroys the test's purpose while saving no round trip (one indexed query either way, on a two-row table).

tests/factories.py:167-168 already emits a single LIMIT 1 query via .all()[0:1]; .first() is the same one query and additionally injects ORDER BY pk on an unordered model. No DB work removed, and the tool itself notes the exception behaviour differs.
test_sso.py:88-89 evaluates User.objects.filter(email=EMAIL) twice (count() then first()); list()-ing it once removes one round trip. Genuine, but it is test code.
